result.raw_final:
A **gluten-free way of eating can fit pregnancy**, but a weight-loss diet generally isn’t appropriate during pregnancy. Please ask your obstetrician or a registered dietitian who specializes in pregnancy to set a healthy weight-gain goal for your starting BMI, pregnancy stage, and health. ACOG’s general guidance is to focus on healthy eating and appropriate gain, rather than trying to lose weight.

Here’s a balanced gluten-free day to discuss with them:

- **Breakfast:** Eggs with spinach, fruit, and certified gluten-free oats or a fortified gluten-free cereal.
- **Lunch:** Quinoa or brown rice bowl with chicken, beans, or tofu; plenty of vegetables; and avocado or olive oil.
- **Snack:** Yogurt with berries and nuts, or hummus with vegetables.
- **Dinner:** Salmon or thoroughly cooked beans, potatoes or brown rice, and cooked vegetables.
- **Drinks:** Water; choose pasteurized dairy or fortified alternatives.

Favor naturally gluten-free foods—vegetables, fruit, beans, lentils, eggs, meat, fish, dairy, rice, potatoes, corn, quinoa, and buckwheat. Gluten-free packaged foods can be low in fiber or enriched nutrients, so check labels and choose fortified options when useful. Continue your prenatal vitamin as prescribed; don’t add supplements or restrict calories without your clinician’s guidance. If you have celiac disease, strict gluten avoidance and attention to nutrient levels are especially important.

**Sources:** [ACOG: Healthy Eating During Pregnancy](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/healthy-eating-during-pregnancy) and [ACOG: Obesity and Pregnancy](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/obesity-and-pregnancy).

FINAL ANSWER: During pregnancy, don’t start a weight-loss diet unless your obstetric clinician specifically recommends a supervised plan. Ask your OB or pregnancy dietitian to set an appropriate weight-gain goal and tailor a gluten-free menu. Build meals around naturally gluten-free whole foods, include protein, produce, and nutritious grains or starches, use a prenatal vitamin as prescribed, and avoid calorie restriction or supplements without medical advice.
